text: It is reported that two secret societies, the membership of which is largely of the criminal class, have joined forces with labour agitators in the Chinese city and sworn allegiance to one of the most notorious labour leaders. It is believed that their intention is to blackmail Chinese firms and shops dealing in foreign goods, and Chinese in foreign employ.

MILL WORKERS STABBED.
Five strike breakers from a Japanese mill have been stabbed in a teashop by loafers, who are probably strikers. Two of the injured men have been removed to hospital.

label: text
text: Gregorenko, who has been arraigned before the Mixed Court on a charge of aiding and abetting Dr. Fortunatoff in an attempted act of bribery, was acquitted when the case was resumed to-day.

label: text
text: The Assessor stated "that the Court was satisfied that a prima facie case had been made out against another person and that an attempt at bribery had been made," but there was not sufficient evidence against the accused.

label: text
text: Halifax (Nova Scotia), August 3. —With a view to terminate the dispute between the British Empire Steel Corporation and the striking coalminers, which has completely stopped work in the coal industry for the past five months and caused much distress and disorder, the Premier, the Hon. H. N. Rhodes, P.C., has proposed that the parties immediately arrange an interim contract for six months to embrace the 1924 working terms and the 1922 wages. Thid Provincial Government will grant a rebate of one-fifth of its coal royalties for a year, and institute a full enquiry. The Executive Pedy, representing the workers, has already recommended that the Unions should accept the proposals.

label: text
text: The welcome to the United States naval visitors grows even more cordial as the end of the visit approaches. Huge crowds revisited the warships to-day. The crush was so great that fifty cases of fainting and slight injury had to be treated.

label: text
text: The Customs authorities have discovered a widespread conspiracy, with head-quarters in Hong Kong and agencies at Australian ports, to smuggle Chinese into Australia. The alleged method is the use of birth certificates of dead Chinese.

label: text

label: text
text: Chinese who have left the employ of foreigners at Wuchow and have remained, are having to justify their existence removing the City wall and building roads, the wage paid them being 60 cents a day.
